Title: Getting started
Summary: A quick guide to using the Gift of the Givers prototype.
Content: Start from the Home page. Use Donate to record a prototype donation, Volunteer to register your interest, Register to create a donor account, and Log in to access your account. Employees can use the seeded employee account to access the employee dashboard in a development/demo environment.

Title: Create a donor account
Summary: Create a donor account and sign in.
Content: Select Register. Enter your first name, last name, email address, and a password of at least 6 characters. The application creates the account with the Donor role and signs you in automatically. Email confirmation is disabled in this prototype.

Title: Make a donation
Summary: Record a one-time or recurring donation in the prototype.
Content: Open Donate, choose One-time or Recurring, select ZAR, USD, or EUR, enter an amount, and optionally select Donate anonymously. Submit the form. The application sends the donation details to the configured Azure Function. If the function succeeds, the returned certificate number is stored with the donation and a certificate page is shown. This prototype does not process real payments.

Title: Donate anonymously
Summary: Record a donation without displaying the signed-in donor name.
Content: On the Donate page, tick Donate anonymously before submitting. The application records the donor name as Anonymous Donor. This is application-level anonymity; it is not a guarantee of anonymity from infrastructure, logs, payment providers, or administrators.

Title: Register as a volunteer
Content: Open Volunteer. Enter your full name, skills, availability, and optionally an email address. Select Register interest. The registration is stored in the SQLite database and a confirmation page is displayed. Employees can later see volunteer sign-ups on the employee dashboard.

Title: Employee login
Summary: Access the employee dashboard in a development/demo environment.
Content: Use the Login page with the seeded employee account documented in the project README. The Employee role is required for the dashboard. Change the seeded password before any real deployment and do not publish demo credentials.

Title: Use the employee dashboard
Summary: View volunteers and publish project updates.
Content: The employee dashboard lists volunteer sign-ups ordered by registration date. Employees can publish a project update by entering a project name and update text. New updates are stored with the signed-in employee name and date, then displayed on the dashboard.

Title: Configure the Azure donation function
Summary: Configure the endpoint used to generate donation certificates.
Content: The application reads AzureFunction:DonationUrl from configuration. The default development value points to a local Azure Functions endpoint. In Azure, configure the setting through the application's environment/configuration rather than hard-coding a production URL. The endpoint is expected to accept a POST JSON payload containing amount, donationType, currency, and isAnonymous and return a certificateNumber.

Title: Database and stored data
Summary: Understand where application data is stored.
Content: The project uses Entity Framework Core with SQLite. The default connection string points to giftofthegivers.db. Donations, volunteers, project updates, and ASP.NET Identity data are stored through ApplicationDbContext. The application calls EnsureCreated at startup, so a missing database is created automatically.

Title: Run the application locally
Summary: Start the ASP.NET Core application during development.
Content: Install the .NET 8 SDK and, if using Visual Studio, the ASP.NET and web development workload. Open GiftoftheGivers.sln, restore packages, build, and run the project. The README recommends Visual Studio 2022 version 17.8 or newer. The app uses HTTPS redirection and the launch settings determine the development address.

Title: Publish to Azure App Service
Summary: Prepare the application for an ASP.NET Core host.
Content: Build a Release publish with dotnet publish -c Release -o publish, then deploy the published output to an ASP.NET Core-capable host such as Azure App Service. Configure the SQLite connection and Azure Function URL through application settings for the target environment. Review database persistence and backup requirements before production use.

Title: Troubleshoot donation failures
Content: If the page says the Azure Donation Function URL has not been configured, set AzureFunction:DonationUrl. If the function returns an HTTP error, check the function endpoint, request contract, authentication/network requirements, and function logs. If no certificate number is returned, verify that the function response contains certificateNumber. The current controller also displays the exception message when it cannot connect.

Title: Troubleshoot login
Content: Confirm the email and password are correct. New donor registrations are assigned the Donor role. The seeded employee must have the Employee role. If the database is reset, the startup seed process recreates the employee account. For production, use a secure password and consider stronger Identity password, lockout, confirmation, and recovery settings.

Title: Production security checklist
Summary: Important hardening steps before real-world use.
Content: Change the seeded employee password. Do not expose credentials in source control or documentation. Use HTTPS and secure application settings. Consider stronger ASP.NET Identity policies, account lockout, email confirmation, password recovery, authorization tests, CSRF protections, validation, structured logging, and secret management. The donation page explicitly states that payment processing is not implemented, so integrate a trusted payment provider before accepting real funds.
